clue.text: Tired wife prepared cake to be eaten by husband and daughter

indicators.note: something eaten by the couple ends up inside them, so the cake goes between H and D
a cake prepared is mixed up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted wife bakes a cake that her husband and daughter then devour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired' is British slang here: whacked means worn out, not beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacked is informal British slang for utterly exhausted, a synonym of tired.

clue.text: Male's acting struggles with screen villains

parts.note: he is a male pronoun; the 's is read as 'is' linking it on
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank
vies means competes or struggles

explanation.surface: A man's performance on screen is hard work alongside the film's bad guys.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavies are the stock villain roles in films and plays, so the plural fits screen villains.

clue.text: Conservative fool stopped by European lawsuits

indicators.note: the fool is plugged by the European letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A Tory idiot is held up by a European over legal actions.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is a legal action brought before a court, so cases are lawsuits.

clue.text: Most convenient direction around? That's south

indicators.note: the direction goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: east is a compass direction
i.e. is short for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone asks which way round is handiest and is told to go south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' stands for i.e., the Latin abbreviation read as 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiest is the superlative of easy, meaning least troublesome or handiest, so most convenient.

clue.text: Footballer's out wide after fine touches

indicators.note: the footballer part comes after the letter for fine

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: out means the wide letter is removed from the footballer

parts.note: a winger is a footballer who plays on the flank; with the 's it gives the plural form
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A footballer playing out wide shows some fine touches on the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footballer's out wide' looks like where the player stands; it actually tells you to drop W from WINGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger something is to touch or handle it, so fingers is a verb synonym of touches.

clue.text: High flyer is buying limousine, say, for all

indicators.note: is takes in the purchase, so the car and certificate go inside

parts.note: a limousine is an example of a car
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: A rich high flyer is buying a limousine for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too close to the sun on wax wings, the original high flyer.

clue.text: Grandpa entertaining party over sponsor?

indicators.note: the grandpa hosts the party, holding it inside

parts.note: grand is G (a thousand) and pa is father, together G plus FATHER

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the party is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An old man hosts a party, then asks whether that makes him a sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grandpa' must be split: a grand is a thousand pounds, written G, and pa is a father.
explanation.definitionFit: A godfather sponsors a child at baptism, vowing to oversee its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Consider secret plan to conceal some money

indicators.note: the rearranged secret hides the penny inside it
a plan arranges things, so the letters of secret are reorganised

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small amount of money

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a covert scheme to hide some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plan' looks like a noun in the surface, but it works as a verb telling you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect something can mean to have regard for it or take it into account, close to consider.

clue.text: Her best lead is lost then found again

indicators.note: letters that are lost are scattered and astray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Her strongest clue goes missing and then turns up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her best lead is' gives exactly the thirteen letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Found here means set up or establish, so to found again is to re-establish an institution.

clue.text: Damn rodents!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of annoyance
second meaning: plural of the rodent

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes it one cry of horror at vermin; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as an irritated exclamation and as the plural name of common long-tailed vermin.

clue.text: Attendant to cook sardines (not in pan)

parts.note: to stew is to cook slowly

indicators.note: not means the word in is subtracted from the sardine letters
to pan is to criticise harshly, knocking the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cabin attendant is told to cook some sardines without using a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking vessel, but here it is the verb meaning to slate, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewardess is a female attendant on a plane or ship, serving passengers.

clue.text: Back in the past I had successful records

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read in reverse
the letters sit inside the words past I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that in former days they had records that sold well.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits are popular, chart-topping songs or recordings, synonyms for successful records.

clue.text: Sang like a pig?

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to police, and a pig's cry is a shrill squeal; both meet in one past-tense verb

explanation.walkthrough: Sang is underworld slang for informed, and an informer also squeals; the pig gives the literal noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both made a pig's high cry and betrayed accomplices, just as sang does in slang.

clue.text: County ignoring Number 10 about Latin being basic

indicators.note: the county ignores the ten, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: Essex is an English county
X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: about signals the letters of Latin are moved around

explanation.surface: An English county snubs Downing Street over its basic Latin teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' looks like the Prime Minister's house; it is just X, the Roman ten. ESSE then takes NTIAL, the rearranged LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means fundamental or indispensable, a near synonym of basic.

clue.text: Celebrity in magazine with diamonds like teeth?

indicators.note: the celebrity sits within the magazine

parts.note: Elle is a fashion magazine
a big name is a celebrity
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A star photographed in a glossy magazine wearing diamonds, with dazzling teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that teeth are coated in enamel by nature, so they are fairly called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth have a hard outer coating called enamel, so they are enamel-coated, hence enamelled.

clue.text: Photographs stolen in seconds

indicators.note: the stolen goods go inside the two seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, doubled for the plural
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Pictures of stolen goods are snapped in moments.
explanation.definitionFit: Shots are snaps taken with a camera, an informal word for photographs.

clue.text: Pick up metal for a bargain

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the metal is taken by its sound

parts.note: steel is a metal alloy

explanation.surface: Someone snaps up some metal cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is informal for something bought at a very low price, a real bargain.

clue.text: Words of praise for butter I spread

indicators.note: spread means the letters are smeared about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone praises the butter they have spread on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like what you do with butter, but it rearranges BUTTER I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an act or statement expressing admiration or gratitude, often spoken praise.

clue.text: Work hard in America after start of exam, worried it's complex

indicators.note: the American work comes after the start of exam
the start of exam is its first letter

parts.note: labor is the American spelling of labour, to work hard
ate, as in ate away at, means worried

explanation.surface: A student works hard but frets that the exam is complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' gives ATE, as in 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate and detailed, with many parts, close to complex.

clue.text: Prizefighter is sure rib is cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A boxer is certain that his rib has cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruiser is a big, tough man, especially a boxer who relies on brute force.

clue.text: Aware of melody above noise

indicators.note: in a down clue above puts the melody before the noise

parts.note: a tune is a melody
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone notices a melody rising over the racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuned in is an idiom for being alert to and understanding what is going on.

clue.text: Dismissed one putting on paper clothes

parts.note: a batter who is dismissed in cricket is out

indicators.note: the one goes on to the paper, placed inside it

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sacked worker gets dressed in paper clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of garments worn together, a complete costume of clothes.

clue.text: Overconfident people — Ernie, Ritchie and Fawkes?

parts.note: Ernie Wise was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise
Guy Ritchie is a film director and Guy Fawkes the Gunpowder Plot conspirator, two Guys

explanation.surface: A comedian, a film director and a plotter are all said to be cocky.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was a British TV comedian; Guy Fawkes tried to blow up Parliament in 1605.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise guys are know-alls who act cocky or smart, people too sure of themselves.

clue.text: Wears DayGlo necklaces on vacation

indicators.note: vacated words are emptied, leaving only their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker puts on fluorescent necklaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' suggests a holiday, but it empties DayGlo and necklaces to their outside letters. DayGlo is a fluorescent paint brand.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on, so dons means puts on or wears.

clue.text: March 2nd: class to retire from military service

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
B is the second class or grade after A

explanation.surface: A date in March and a class of soldiers leaving the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March 2nd' reads as a date, but March is a protest demo and 2nd class is B.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob is the informal British verb for releasing someone from the armed forces, short for demobilise.

clue.text: Sportsmen untroubled by heat?

parts.note: a heat is a preliminary round; competitors who come through one comfortably go on to the next stage

explanation.walkthrough: Heat looks like hot weather, but in athletics a heat is a qualifying race, and those who get through it untroubled advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors who win through a preliminary round to the next stage of a contest are so called.

clue.text: Arranged for servant's delivery

indicators.note: a speaker's delivery is how words are spoken, so the servant is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: Plans are set up to have the maid sent along.
explanation.definitionFit: Made, as in made plans or made the bed, can mean fixed up or prepared, hence arranged.

clue.text: Victor learned to extract uranium for green stones

parts.note: V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the uranium is extracted, taken out of the learned word

parts.note: erudite means learned
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A scholar named Victor learns how to mine uranium from green rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdite is a green ornamental rock from southern Africa, carved into ornaments, so the stones fit.

clue.text: It's on the captain to equip team

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
a band is a group or team of people

explanation.surface: It is the captain's job to kit out the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'it's the captain's responsibility', but it means the item worn on the captain's sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports captain wears a distinguishing band around the upper sleeve marking the role.
